problem:
Problem description
- There is a daily staffing planning problem for a periodic service over a horizon of $$T$$ consecutive time periods, indexed by $$t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$$.
- The service requires a minimum number of active personnel in each period, given by the demand vector $$d_t$$ for each period $$t$$.
- Each worker starts at the beginning of one allowed start period and works continuously for a fixed shift length of $$L$$ periods.
- A worker assigned to a start period contributes coverage to every period within that shift window, including periods that wrap around the end of the daily horizon if the schedule is cyclic.
- The planning objective is to choose the smallest feasible staffing plan, meaning the minimum total number of scheduled workers, while meeting all period-by-period demand requirements.
- The model may use a uniform staffing cost $$c$$ per scheduled worker, or period-dependent start costs $$c_t$$ if differentiated costs are needed.
- Each active worker contributes coverage capacity $$q$$ per covered period, with the standard case being a single unit of coverage per worker per period.
- Required business constraints:
  - Every time period must have enough active workers to meet or exceed the required demand in that period.
  - Workers can only start at permitted start periods.
  - Each worker follows the fixed shift length $$L$$ once scheduled.
  - Shift coverage must be counted consistently across the daily cycle, including any wrap-around periods.
  - Staffing quantities must be nonnegative integers.
- A solution is represented by:
  - $$x_t$$: the number of workers whose shifts start at the beginning of period $$t$$.
  - $$z$$: the total number of workers scheduled over the day, used as the objective value.
  - Optionally, a coverage summary by period may be reported as a derived result from $$x_t$$.

Input Format
{
  "T": "Integer parameter denoting the number of planning periods in the daily horizon, written as $$T$$.",
  "L": "Integer parameter denoting the fixed shift length in periods, written as $$L$$.",
  "demand": {
    "shape": "[$$T$$]",
    "type": "array of integers",
    "meaning": "The required staffing level in each period, where element $$d_t$$ is the demand for period $$t$$."
  },
  "start_cost": {
    "shape": "scalar or [$$T$$]",
    "type": "numeric",
    "meaning": "Optional staffing cost parameter, written as $$c$$ or $$c_t$$, for starting one worker in a period."
  },
  "coverage_capacity": {
    "shape": "scalar",
    "type": "numeric",
    "meaning": "Coverage contributed by one active worker in a covered period, written as $$q$$."
  },
  "cyclic_horizon": {
    "shape": "scalar",
    "type": "boolean",
    "meaning": "Indicates whether shifts that extend past the last period wrap around to the beginning of the next daily cycle."
  },
  "periods": {
    "shape": "[$$T$$]",
    "type": "array of objects",
    "meaning": "Optional descriptive labels for each period, including the period index $$t$$ and its time window."
  }
}

Output Format
{
  "start_counts": {
    "shape": "[$$T$$]",
    "type": "array of nonnegative integers",
    "meaning": "The number of workers starting at each period, denoted by $$x_t$$."
  },
  "total_workers": {
    "shape": "scalar",
    "type": "integer",
    "meaning": "The total number of scheduled workers over the planning horizon, denoted by $$z$$."
  }
}

Example(s)

Input 1
{
  "T": 6,
  "L": 2,
  "demand": [60, 70, 60, 50, 20, 30],
  "coverage_capacity": 1,
  "cyclic_horizon": true,
  "periods": [
    { "index": 1, "time": "06:00-10:00", "required_staff": 60 },
    { "index": 2, "time": "10:00-14:00", "required_staff": 70 },
    { "index": 3, "time": "14:00-18:00", "required_staff": 60 },
    { "index": 4, "time": "18:00-22:00", "required_staff": 50 },
    { "index": 5, "time": "22:00-02:00", "required_staff": 20 },
    { "index": 6, "time": "02:00-06:00", "required_staff": 30 }
  ]
}

parameters.name: periods
parameters.description: Optional descriptive objects for period t, including index and time window

parameters.name: planning_periods
parameters.description: Integer number of planning periods in the cyclic horizon

parameters.name: demand
parameters.description: Required staffing level in each period

parameters.name: coverage_capacity
parameters.description: Coverage capacity contributed by one active worker in a covered period

parameters.name: uniform_start_cost
parameters.description: Optional uniform cost per scheduled worker

parameters.name: start_cost
parameters.description: Optional period-dependent start cost for starting one worker in period t

parameters.name: cyclic_horizon
parameters.description: Boolean indicating whether shift coverage wraps around the end of the horizon

variables.name: start_counts
variables.description: Nonnegative integer number of workers whose shifts start at each period

variables.name: total_workers
variables.description: Total number of workers scheduled over the planning horizon

constraints.name: nonnegative_integer_start_counts
constraints.description: Start counts must be nonnegative integers for each planning period

constraints.name: nonnegative_integer_total_workers
constraints.description: Total workers must be a nonnegative integer

constraints.name: period_demand_coverage
constraints.description: Each period t must have total active coverage at least the required demand, with explicit linear cyclic indexing

constraints.name: fixed_length_shift_assignment
constraints.description: Redundant semantic statement that each scheduled worker starts in exactly one period and works a fixed contiguous shift of length L; retained as a modeling note only

constraints.name: cyclic_wraparound_coverage
constraints.description: Coverage indices wrap around the horizon when the horizon is cyclic; this is already embedded in the explicit coverage family

constraints.name: total_workers_derived_from_starts
constraints.description: The total number of scheduled workers equals the sum of all start counts

objectives.name: minimize_total_scheduled_workers
objectives.description: Minimize the total number of scheduled workers over the planning horizon

objectives.name: minimize_total_staffing_cost
objectives.description: If differentiated start costs are used, minimize the total staffing cost based on uniform or period-dependent start costs while satisfying all demand requirements

final_objective.description: Minimize the total number of scheduled workers over the planning horizon, using the derived aggregate total_workers.
